summary: Customer A is currently classified as High Risk due to the accumulation of five distinct early-warning signals, including significant revenue decline, negative cash flow, and collateral devaluation. The customer's financial health is further pressured by a downturn in the seafood industry and contagion risk from a related company, An Phat Garment Co., which is currently past due.

findings.statement: Customer A experienced a 20.6% drop in 90-day revenue compared to the baseline average.
The customer has reported negative net cash flow for two consecutive periods, with the most recent at -855.3.
Related company An Phat Garment Co. is currently 17 days past due, indicating potential contagion risk.
Collateral value for the machinery has decreased by 10.8% from its peak value.
The seafood industry is experiencing a downturn with a growth rate of -6.1%.

recommended_actions.rationale: The customer has triggered 5 early-warning signals, requiring monthly monitoring per policy P-17.
Collateral value has dropped by more than 10%, necessitating a request for additional collateral or a credit limit reduction per policy P-22.
A related company is past due, requiring a formal review of contagion risk and repayment capacity per policy P-31.

limitations: The credit officer should verify if the negative cash flow is a temporary seasonal effect or a structural issue and confirm the extent of the financial dependency between Customer A and An Phat Garment Co..
